claim: The retrospective cohort's Table 1 reports diagnostic turnaround time (TAT) of 51.1 minutes (median; IQR 41.1–65.0) for 23,718 analyzed ED visits. Methods define TAT as elapsed time from ED order of the standardized laboratory panel to the last result of all panel tests reported in the EHR. It therefore spans order-to-laboratory arrival and laboratory processing/reporting, and does not isolate active work from queue, transport, or processing time. The cohort comprised adult visits at University Medical Center Utrecht, Netherlands, with the standard 14-test internal-medicine laboratory panel ordered, from January 2017 through January 2020. Repeated visits were separate events and the first qualifying panel order per visit was used. Of 24,727 eligible visits, 290 with incomplete performed tests, 6 with ambiguous daylight-saving transition times, and 713 outlier-trimmed visits (2.9%) were excluded, leaving 23,718. This is an elapsed diagnostic TAT summary, not an intrinsic active-work distribution, report-review interval, or generic default.
